solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Award from king returned — name black (4)

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned is sent back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the OBE is an honour conferred by the monarch

annotation.surface: A monarch hands back an honour and names someone in disgrace.
annotation.walkthrough: The OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is an honour the British monarch confers. Ebon is a poetic word for black.
annotation.definitionFit: Ebon is the literary form of ebony, meaning black.

entries.clue: Religious order country earl accommodates (11)

indicatorNotes.accommodates: to accommodate is to take in, so BENIN plus E holds the order inside

blocks.note: an edict is an order; it sits between BEN and INE

annotation.surface: A religious order is housed by a country's aristocrat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Religious order' reads as one phrase, but 'Religious' alone is the definition: as a noun, a religious is a monk or nun, and 'order' is the edict.
annotation.definitionFit: A Benedictine is a monk or nun of St Benedict's order, and a religious (noun) is any such person.

entries.clue: Mentioned by name in letter, Mrs Harker died (9)

indicatorNotes.in: Mrs Harker goes in the letter, so NOTE wraps MINA

blocks.note: a note is a short letter
Mina Harker, heroine of Bram Stoker's Dracula

annotation.surface: A letter reports the death of Mina Harker, named in it.
annotation.walkthrough: Mina Harker is Jonathan Harker's wife in Dracula, and Dracula is itself told in letters, which is what makes the surface so neat.
annotation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put their name forward, so a nominated candidate has been named for the post.

entries.clue: Almodóvar’s White House an Oscar winner (10)

indicatorNotes.Almodóvar’s: Pedro Almodóvar is a Spanish director, so his words for white and house are Spanish

blocks.note: blanca is Spanish for white; Spanish puts the adjective after the noun

annotation.surface: A Spanish film-maker's grand residence wins an Academy Award.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a Spanish take on the US president's residence; the Spanish words go in Spanish order, noun first.
annotation.definitionFit: Casablanca (1942) won the Oscar for Best Picture.

entries.clue: Instrument Cretan occasionally carries in case (7)

indicatorNotes.occasionally: only now and then, so every other letter of Cretan
indicatorNotes.carries: the letters CEA carry the next word inside them

blocks.note: C, E, A: the first, third and fifth letters of CRETAN
lest = in case, as in 'lest we forget'; it goes between CE and A

annotation.surface: A man from Crete now and then brings along something in a carrying case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In case' looks like the container, the Cretan carrying something in a case, but it is the word LEST.
annotation.definitionFit: The celesta is a keyboard instrument with bell-like tones, heard in the Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy.

entries.clue: Landmark in west, yet built for east, needs moving (6,2,7)

indicatorNotes.needs moving: the letters must be moved about

annotation.surface: A monument in the West was really made for the East and has to be relocated.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nods to history: the statue was built in France, to the east, and shipped across the Atlantic.
annotation.definitionFit: The Statue of Liberty stands in New York harbour, a landmark of the West.

entries.clue: Fail when beginning to test hollow material (7)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of test, its first letter

blocks.note: to bomb is to fail badly
as = when, as in 'as I left'

annotation.surface: An exam paper is failed right at the start because its material is empty.
annotation.walkthrough: Bombast first meant cotton padding for clothes, which is why 'material' fits: empty, puffed-up words are stuffing.
annotation.definitionFit: Bombast is high-sounding language with little substance, literally once padding material.

entries.clue: Sequence seen in ciné verité? Surely not! (5)

indicatorNotes.Sequence seen in: a run of letters that can be seen inside the phrase

annotation.surface: A film buff watches a scene in a documentary-style movie and can't believe it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sequence' is a film word, a run of shots, so it passes as part of the cinema surface while telling you to take a run of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Never!' is an exclamation of disbelief, like 'Surely not!'

entries.clue: Advisers must have name for island chain (5)

indicatorNotes.must have: the advisers must take on the name letter
indicatorNotes.for: N stands in for I, replacing it

blocks.note: i = island; N replaces it in AIDES

annotation.surface: Consultants insist on naming a chain of islands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Island chain' reads as one phrase, an archipelago; the definition is 'chain' alone, a chain of mountains.
annotation.definitionFit: The Andes are the mountain chain running down western South America.

entries.clue: Work man excited about the writer’s Alfa Romeo (6,4)

indicatorNotes.excited: stirred up, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged letters go around the writer's word

blocks.note: the writer is = I'M; it sits after the AN of the rearranged letters
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A man gets worked up about the author's Italian sports car.
annotation.walkthrough: The Alfa Romeo reads as a car; Alfa is used as it is spelt while Romeo is the radio code for R. The answer is Orwell's novel.
annotation.definitionFit: Animal Farm is a work by George Orwell, a work in the sense of a book.

entries.clue: Roman poet initially offered six denarii (4)

indicatorNotes.initially: at first, so the first letter of offered

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
d stood for denarii, the old British penny abbreviation

annotation.surface: A poet in ancient Rome is first offered six silver coins.
annotation.walkthrough: The pre-1971 British penny was written d, from the Roman denarius, so the Roman coins in the surface give D.
annotation.definitionFit: Ovid wrote the Metamorphoses in Augustan Rome.

entries.clue: Handsome young man said no unfortunately (6)

indicatorNotes.unfortunately: things went wrong, so the letters fall into a new order

annotation.surface: A good-looking young man proposed, and sadly she turned him down.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a romantic rejection, and the handsome man turns out to be the very one who was refused.
annotation.definitionFit: Adonis, the youth loved by Aphrodite, is the byword for a handsome young man.

entries.clue: An Italian meets with war god unexpectedly (8)

blocks.note: Ares, the Greek god of war

annotation.surface: An Italian runs into the god of war without warning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'An Italian' reads as a person, but it asks for the Italian word for 'an'.
annotation.definitionFit: Unawares means without warning, as in 'caught unawares'.

entries.clue: Film star and French guy she loves going round wood (5,6)

indicatorNotes.going round: HERMAN goes round the wood, holding ELM after its H

blocks.note: her man = the guy she loves
elm is a wood; it goes inside HERMAN after the H

annotation.surface: A screen star and a Frenchman her heart belongs to are walking around a wood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French guy' looks like a unit, a Frenchman, but 'French' goes with 'and' to make ET, and 'guy' starts HER MAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Merman made her name on Broadway but also starred in Hollywood musicals such as Call Me Madam.

entries.clue: Second division game’s end? (4)

annotation.surface: A question about the end of a match in football's second tier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second division' reads as a football league; here game means hunted animals, and the end of a rabbit or deer is its tail.
annotation.definitionFit: A scut is the short tail of a hare, rabbit or deer, animals hunted as game.

entries.clue: One of O’Toole’s characters? (10)

blocks.note: the surface reading: a role played by the actor Peter O'Toole, such as Lawrence of Arabia
the setter's reading: characters are printed symbols, so look at the name as typed, O’Toole’s, and ask which symbol it has two of

annotation.surface: A question about a role played by the actor Peter O'Toole.
annotation.walkthrough: Characters suggests roles, Lawrence of Arabia and the rest, but it means typed symbols: O’Toole’s, as printed, contains apostrophes.
annotation.definitionFit: The clue reads straight once characters means typed symbols: the printed name O’Toole’s contains two of this punctuation mark.

entries.clue: Subdued reviews appearing in newspaper column (9)

indicatorNotes.appearing in: the reviews appear inside the column

blocks.note: an op-ed is an opinion column opposite the editorial page
the press a show gets is its reviews; it goes between OP and ED

annotation.surface: Muted notices turn up in a newspaper's opinion column.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Subdued reviews' reads as lukewarm notices, but 'Subdued' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a people ground down by harsh rule are both kept under and subdued.

entries.clue: Show Conservative popular articles in German, Spanish and French (10)

annotation.surface: A popular Tory programme translated into three European languages.
annotation.walkthrough: Cinderella is the most-performed British pantomime, the family Christmas stage show; the three definite articles run in the order the languages are listed.
annotation.definitionFit: Cinderella is a show, most often staged as a Christmas pantomime.

entries.clue: Writing perhaps in unfinished book, American figure (7)

indicatorNotes.unfinished: HOME is left without its last letter

blocks.note: writing is one of the three Rs, with reading and arithmetic
in = at home, HOME, cut short

annotation.surface: Some text in a half-written book, an American character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a link telling you where the writing goes, but it is the word itself: in means at home.
annotation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a geometric figure, a four-sided shape with equal sides.

entries.clue: No professional couple to be found in a once important city (7)

indicatorNotes.to be found in: the couple is found inside A UR

annotation.surface: No working pair can be found in a city that used to matter.
annotation.walkthrough: Ur is the crossword's favourite ancient city, once the great city of Sumer.
annotation.definitionFit: An amateur is no professional: someone who does it unpaid.

entries.clue: None too bright taking drink after parking (4)

indicatorNotes.after: the drink comes after the parking letter

blocks.note: P is the road-sign letter for parking

annotation.surface: Someone not very clever has a drink after leaving the car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'None too bright' reads as dim-witted, but it means dim in colour.
annotation.definitionFit: Bright here means vivid in colour, and a washed-out shade lacks that vividness.

entries.clue: Sacrifice Banquo’s end Macbeth arranged (8)

indicatorNotes.end: the end of Banquo is its last letter
indicatorNotes.arranged: to arrange things is to set them out in a chosen order, so the letters of Macbeth are laid out afresh

annotation.surface: Macbeth arranges the killing of Banquo, a sacrifice to his ambition.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the plot of the play: Macbeth has Banquo murdered. Hecate is also a character in Macbeth, hiding in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A hecatomb is a great public sacrifice, originally of a hundred oxen.

entries.clue: Tracks in road crash with top pulled down (5)

indicatorNotes.with top pulled down: in a down clue the top letter is pulled to the bottom

blocks.note: a shunt is a minor car collision; its S moves from top to bottom

annotation.surface: Wheel marks on the road after a collision in which a car's roof was crushed.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang a shunt is a minor car crash, usually a rear-end bump. 'Tracks' looks like tyre tracks, but it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To track someone is to hunt them, so he hunts = he tracks.

entries.clue: What is carried by famous vessel, heading for Colchis? (5)

indicatorNotes.heading for: the head, or first letter, of Colchis
indicatorNotes.by: the C is set by the ship's name, next to it

annotation.surface: A question about what the Argo carried on its voyage to Colchis.
annotation.walkthrough: Jason sailed the Argo to Colchis for the Golden Fleece, so the surface is a real Greek myth; the whole clue also works as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods a ship carries.

entries.clue: Everything involves biblical character in test (1,5)

indicatorNotes.involves: to involve is to include, so ALL holds EVE

blocks.note: Eve, the first woman; she goes between AL and L

annotation.surface: A Bible figure turns up throughout an exam.
annotation.walkthrough: An A level is the British school-leaving exam taken at about 18, the one that decides university places.
annotation.definitionFit: An A level is an exam, a test, in a single subject.

entries.clue: Fate of William I say in mother’s absence? (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the letters of mother are to be taken out of it
indicatorNotes.absence: the mother is absent, so MA is removed

blocks.note: William I was a Norman; say marks him as an example

annotation.surface: A question about what became of William the Conqueror without his mum.
annotation.walkthrough: The Norns are the three Fates of Norse myth, so one Norn is a Fate.
annotation.definitionFit: Norse myth has three Norns spinning the threads of destiny, matching the three Greek Fates.

entries.clue: Heavy mob endures in battle (10)

indicatorNotes.in battle: letters locked in battle are thrown about

annotation.surface: A heavy crowd holds out in combat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavy mob' reads as a phrase, British slang for thugs or riot police; the definition is 'Heavy' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Something burdensome is heavy, a weight to carry.

entries.clue: Prophet very different: state’s intervention needed? (10)

indicatorNotes.intervention needed: an intervention comes between, so the state word must go inside SO OTHER

blocks.note: to state is to say; it goes between SO OTH and ER

annotation.surface: A seer is quite unlike the rest: is government meddling called for?
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' reads as the government, but it is the verb, to say.
annotation.definitionFit: A soothsayer claims to tell what is coming, which is the old sense of prophet.

entries.clue: Accomplished daughter regularly taking MDMA (4)

blocks.note: to be on a drug is to take it regularly
E = ecstasy, the street name for MDMA

annotation.surface: A gifted daughter has a habit of using ecstasy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like the alternate-letters signal, but the letters of 'daughter' do not help; it goes with 'taking' to mean on.
annotation.definitionFit: Done means accomplished, as in 'job done'.
